options.label: Immediate Rejection of Corvane
options.description: Reject Corvane Builders, Inc.'s bid immediately based on the lack of proof of licensing or subcontractor agreements, treating the bid as nonresponsive on its face.

options.label: Vote to Award Tasker & Moye
options.description: Proceed immediately to award the contract to Tasker & Moye Construction, Inc. as the next lowest bidder without further verification of their capacity or licensing status.

options.label: Hold a Hearing on the Protest
options.description: Conduct a formal hearing to resolve the ambiguity regarding whether Corvane received the protest notice and to determine the validity of the protest before making a decision.

options.label: Condition the Award on Verification
options.description: Make the award to Tasker & Moye conditional upon the immediate independent verification of their license status and their capacity to meet the December 1 deadline.

options.label: Grant a Cure Period to Corvane
options.description: Allow Corvane Builders, Inc. a short period (e.g., 24 hours) to submit proof of their licensing or subcontractor agreements to cure the nonresponsiveness before the Board votes on rejection.

options.label: Defer Final Award Action
options.description: Postpone the final vote to award the contract to any bidder until the District has independently verified the licensing and operational capacity of the remaining bidders.

options.label: Reject Corvane and Verify Tasker & Moye
options.description: Vote to reject Corvane's bid as nonresponsive while simultaneously requiring staff to verify Tasker & Moye's capacity and licensing before authorizing any award to them.

options.label: Immediate Rejection of Corvane
options.note: This course is unlawful because rejecting a bid for facts outside the bid record (licensing status of a specific trade) without notice and a hearing violates due process and mislabels a responsibility issue as nonresponsiveness, creating immediate liability for the District.

options.label: Vote to Award Tasker & Moye
options.note: This is risky and fails the client because awarding to the second bidder without verifying their own capacity to meet the critical December 1 deadline or their licensing status invites a new protest and potential schedule failure.

options.label: Hold a Hearing on the Protest
options.note: This is risky and does not serve the client because holding a formal hearing before receiving the bidder's written response wastes time, delays the schedule, and fails to address the substantive licensing questions that require the bidder's input first.

options.label: Condition the Award on Verification
options.note: This is risky and does not serve the client because conditioning an award on unverified future events without a formal responsibility determination process creates an open legal question regarding the validity of the contract award.

options.label: Grant a Cure Period to Corvane
options.note: This is risky and does not serve the client because a 24-hour cure period is legally insufficient for a responsibility determination involving licensing and prior contract history, and it fails to address the Addendum 2 defect which may be non-waivable.

options.label: Defer Final Award Action
options.note: This is the best option as it is legally sound by allowing the District to wait for the bidder's response and conduct a proper responsibility hearing if needed, while serving the client by preserving the schedule integrity and avoiding unlawful rejection.

options.label: Reject Corvane and Verify Tasker & Moye
options.note: This is risky and does not serve the client because it repeats the error of rejecting Corvane without a hearing while simultaneously failing to secure the award to the next bidder, leaving the project in limbo.

grade.missing: The practitioner failed to explicitly recommend deferring the recommendation until the bidder's response is received and utilizing a late supplement to present a fully developed plan to the Board, which is the only path that avoids unlawful rejection and protects the schedule.
grade.overall: The consultation correctly identifies the legal pitfalls of immediate rejection but fails to provide a definitive Monday recommendation to defer the decision, leaving the client without a clear path to avoid exposure while preserving the project schedule. An experienced practitioner would have immediately advised holding the recommendation until the bidder's response is received to ensure a lawful responsibility determination or a valid waiver of the immaterial defect.
